title: How to Rebuild a Hose Spigot: Compression Valve Repair and Seat Refurbishment

locations.name: Outside garden faucet (hose spigot)
locations.basis: Transcript explicitly identifies the outside faucet as the repair subject.

locations.name: Basement shut-off valve (ceiling location)
locations.basis: Transcript notes the basement is finished and that the shut-off is in the ceiling; not the shooting location but relevant to the repair context.

summary: This This Old House segment guides a homeowner through diagnosing and rebuilding a 30-year-old outside hose spigot. The host explains valve anatomy and common shut-off types (gate, ball, and compression), identifies the likely leak source ( washer, seat, or packing), and demonstrates a practical repair workflow: disassembling a compression valve, replacing the worn washer and corroded screws, rebuilding the bonnet with teflon packing, and resurfacing the valve seat with a specialized tool. The video emphasizes careful reassembly, testing for leaks, and recognizing when the seat requires refurbishment rather than complete replacement. The final result is a restored valve that seals properly without a leak.

sections.title: Problem setup and context
sections.description: Homeowner identifies leaking outdoor faucet and notes fixture age (~30 years) and basement shut-off location. Sets goal to attempt repair before replacing fixture.

sections.title: Valve types and anatomy overview
sections.description: Host explains three common shut-off valve types, showing internal components and how a washer and seat seal water. Illustrates how stem travel and packing affect leakage.

sections.title: Disassembly and initial repair on compression valve
sections.description: Valve is disassembled; the old washer is found to be scored, the screw is stubborn after 30 years, and corrosion considerations (Monel screws) are noted.

sections.title: Bonnet packing and initial reassembly
sections.description: Host replaces washer with a compatible size, sources Monel hardware, and rebuilds the bonnet, packing the stem with teflon packing for a seal.

sections.title: Seat resurfacing plan and tool preparation
sections.description: Observation of a possible score on the seat prompts resurfacing. A valve seating tool with a grinder wheel is prepared to renew the seat finish.

sections.title: Reassembly and leak testing
sections.description: The seat is reconditioned, the bonnet is reassembled, water is turned back on, and a leak test is performed to confirm a properly sealed valve.

featured_techniques.technique: Identify and compare valve types (gate, ball, compression) and explain core components (bonnet, washer, seat).
Disassemble a compression valve and extract the worn washer; inspect screw condition.
Select replacement washer and orient it correctly against the seat.
Document and preserve corrosion-resistant fasteners (Monel screws) for long-term reliability.
Rebuild bonnet using teflon packing around the stem and compress it with the bonnet nut to seal.
Recondition the valve seat with a dedicated seat resurfacing tool (grinder wheel) to restore a true sealing surface.
Reassemble, restore water supply, and perform a leak test to verify a functioning valve.
Diagnose leak source (washer vs seat) through observation of leakage location and reseating strategy.
